messages:
Raj K.: FYI customer reported requests landing on the fallback route even though `x-tenant-id` is present in the upstream headers. decision logs show a no-match. attaching snippet below.

Maya L.: Can you paste the trace id and the decision log sample? quick check: are we sampling those routes?

Raj K.: trace_id=0x9f3a. decision_log entry for that request:
```
route_eval: {
  match: false,
  rules_checked: [prefilter, header_matcher],
  sampled: true,
  headers_seen: {"host": "api.acme.com", "user-agent": "curl/7.86.0"}
}
```
Note: `x-tenant-id` is NOT in headers_seen. Upstream did include it.

Samir: Hmm, sampler shows `sampled: true` but headers_seen missing tenant header. Could be the samplers run before header normalization/override step. We recently moved header overrides to pre-match hook for perf, might have regressed ordering.

Maya L.: If overrides are applied after sampling, decision logger won't capture the normalized header. That matches. Any chance the gateway strips `x-tenant-id` earlier?

Raj K.: I captured raw proxy logs — upstream sent `x-tenant-id: acme-42`. Proxy logs show it arriving. So removal happens inside the route-eval pipeline.

infra-bot: Deploy started: feature/route-eval-ordering-fix -> staging (build 7761) :rocket:

Samir: Two quick options: A) move sampling after header normalization (safer for observability but slightly more CPU in hot path) B) change decision-log to include an explicit list of normalized fields that are attached at the end of evaluation (append-only, cheaper). Thoughts on perf/PII?

Maya L.: We need to consider PII — some headers may contain tokens. We should NOT blindly log full headers. Option B with an allowlist looks reasonable: e.g., capture canonical headers `x-tenant-id`, `x-route-hash`. Add a size cap.

Raj K.: Agreed. Also UX request from support: console should show whether a field was "present upstream", "dropped pre-eval", or "not-sampled". Right now traces just show absence which confuses customers.

Samir: Proposal: add `decision_log.capture_headers_allowlist` (list of header names), `decision_log.max_header_bytes` (e.g., 1024), and `decision_log.attach_stage` enum {pre_match, post_normalize}. Default: allowlist empty, attach_stage=post_normalize. Also add `trace.meta.header_origin` values to explain origin (upstream|normalized|dropped|not-captured).

Maya L.: Console UX: new column in route trace expanded view "Header captures" that shows allowlisted values and a small legend for header_origin. Also flag sampled vs unsampled traces. We should surface sampling policy and whether the trace was artificially upsampled for debugging.

Raj K.: Edge case: when sampling drops full decision log but we upsample for debug toggle, we must ensure we can request a one-off live capture without increasing global traffic. Maybe implement a per-call `x-debug-capture: true` that bypasses sampling but must be allowed by tenant policy/entitlement.

Samir: I like per-call debug but must be gated: only available for dedicated/private customers or via an admin feature flag for hosted. Audit logs must record who enabled it.

Maya L.: Can we do a short experiment: enable allowlist ["x-tenant-id"] on staging + set attach_stage=post_normalize for 24h and add a temporary route-inspector toggle "capture headers (staging only)" that forces full capture for that session. Monitor CPU change and log sizes.

Samir: I'll open a small RFC and a canary rollout plan. TL;DR of plan in this thread: 1) Add allowlist + size cap. 2) Default to post_normalize. 3) Add header_origin annotations in decision logs. 4) Console: expose toggle + legend + sampled flag. 5) Add `x-debug-capture` gated by entitlement. 6) Canary on staging for 24h then controlled rollout.

Raj K.: Sounds good. Please include a migration note: historical decision logs won't have header_origin, so console should show "unknown" and not claim absence.

infra-bot: Deploy succeeded: feature/route-eval-ordering-fix -> staging (build 7761) :white_check_mark:

Maya L.: I'll prototype the console column today. Can someone add me to the RFC?

Samir: RFC: https://redwood/internal/rfcs/route-decision-header-capture (draft). Added you, Maya.

Raj K.: For follow-up: if staging looks good, recommend short maintenance window to flip default allowlist for a subset of tenants. We'll monitor ingress log sizes and the console storage impact.

Maya L.: :thumbsup: thanks everyone.

Samir: Filed a small issue: infra/7761 -> PERF-2043 (track any CPU regression from moving sampling).

Raj K.: Marking this resolved in thread for now — will re-open if staging shows problems. :eyes:
